main_issue: How Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling sambal belacan without the smell disturbing A's calls, B's room and C's laundry

A-B.evidence: A proposed an after-7pm or weekend timing (5) and B said it didn't fix the problem (8). B then proposed a heads-up (12) and said 'we have a plan' (20).

A-C.evidence: A wanted no strong-smelling cooking; C raised laundry (3), and both accepted the final arrangement (7, 18). A never spoke to the laundry-night rule.

A-D.evidence: D resisted at first (4), then accepted A's proposal: 'after 7 p.m. is fine. Or weekends' (6). A thanked D (7).

B-C.evidence: C said 'Exactly' to B's objection that timing makes no difference (9), and both then accepted the plan (18, 20).

B-D.evidence: B rejected the timing fix (8). B proposed a heads-up and D replied 'Okay, Agent B, I can do that' (12-13).

C-D.evidence: C said a heads-up doesn't help the laundry and asked D to cook on non-laundry nights (16). D: 'I can cook it on the other nights' (17). C: 'That works' (18).
